Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the required wake-visual inspection skill, then inspect current/inherited rollout evidence before touching the target policy. I’ll keep the work strictly within this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult neighboring runs or repository history.

The visual-first skill is applicable because the sampled evaluations include wake keyframes. I’m now anchoring those images to the full score/trajectory/diagnostic record and the inherited optimizer guidance; the policy will remain unchanged until that comparison and the candidate-specific notes are written.

The sampled set contains no semantic failure: all four reach the target. Its useful contrast is the gain-1.7 best rollout versus three deterministic gain-1.9 regressions; the inherited gain-1.725 interpolation is an additional negative result. I’m inspecting the common prewarm first, then those released sheets, as required by the visual-first workflow.

The visual and diagnostic evidence rules out another bearing-gain interpolation: the inherited 1.725 rollout regressed more than both 1.7 and 1.9 despite retaining capture. I’ll record that negative lesson and isolate one new axis—slightly stronger posterior damping—while keeping the evaluated gait, bearing gain, curvature bound, and two-joint steering structure fixed.

The single candidate now changes only `tail_damping` from 0.65 to 0.70; the policy schema and all proven steering/propulsion values remain intact. I’m invoking the prescribed checker now, beginning with the semantic guidance comparison, then the Julia contract and workspace boundary checks—no CFD rollout.

The first prescribed check exposed a workspace-rendering issue rather than a content failure: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice as “copied to guidance,” while the checker requires exactly one marker. I’m inspecting the checker’s comparison logic and immutable/editable boundaries so I can repair this without weakening the evidence test or altering unrelated solver files.

The guidance check now passes after removing the duplicated identical parent marker from the rendered README. The Julia contract command itself did not execute because `julia` is absent from the current PATH (the policy did not fail); I’m checking for the workspace’s configured Julia launcher before treating that as an environment limitation.

The boundary check passes. To satisfy the workspace’s explicit “invoke check-runner” requirement, I’m handing the final independent validation to the configured check-runner role; it will rerun the three prescribed checks and report only evidence-backed PASS/FAIL results.
